```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

MEXGB combines flexible fixed effects with subject-specific random effects.
The Gaussian model assumes independent residuals conditional on these effects.

```{r gaussian}
library(MEXGB)
set.seed(10)
d <- simLong(8, 6, time_points = 4, rho_W = 0)
X <- as.matrix(d[paste0("Var", 1:6)])
Z <- as.matrix(d[c("RandomIntercept", "RandomSlope")])
fit <- MEXGB(X, d$Y, d$id, Z, time = d$time,
             ntree = 10, iter = 2, inner = 2, crossfit = 2,
             linear = FALSE, screen = "none", verbose = FALSE)
fit
head(predict(fit, X, Z, d$id, d$time))
```

The small iteration budget illustrates the interface, not convergence or model
accuracy. For a substantive analysis increase the budget and inspect diagnostics.

For unseen subjects, random effects are zero but population coefficients of `Z`
are retained:

```{r new-subject}
head(predict(fit, X, Z, d$id + 100, d$time))
summary(fit)
```

Use `family = "binomial"` with a numeric 0/1 outcome or `family = "cox"` with a
two-column matrix of positive observed times and 0/1 status (1 means event).
Right-censored `survival::Surv` inputs are also supported. Start-stop and interval
censoring are not. Cox rows represent clustered event times rather than repeated
time-varying records for one terminal event. `type = "survival"` returns a matrix
of conditional survival probabilities for requested `times`.

For nonlinear links, zero-random-effect predictions are not marginal predictions
integrated over the random-effects distribution. The Cox update uses a Poisson
working approximation. Failed Laplace optimizations warn, retain the PQL update,
and appear in `laplace_diagnostics`.

## Evaluation

Within-subject folds tune predictions for additional observations of represented
subjects. They are not subject-held-out validation or temporal validation.
Adaptive choices share these folds; evaluate final performance on an independent
test set or with nested validation tailored to the task. Never report the training
predictions above as external validation performance.

## Simulation

`simLong()` generates Gaussian, binary or clustered event-time data. Binary and
survival discrimination targets are solved on a finite pilot; achieved pilot
values do not guarantee exact population or realised-sample discrimination.
Survival censoring rates are calibrated on the realised sample. Gaussian
simulations with nonzero `rho_W` include residual serial correlation beyond that
modelled by MEXGB and can be used to study misspecification.
